enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1017 PM MST Thu Nov 12 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1100 PM MST Thu Nov 12 2026

 - A Pacific cold front will arrive Friday evening, bringing
   scattered rain showers overnight into Saturday. A few bands of
   heavier rain will be possible, especially across West Texas.

 - Breezy and cooler on Saturday, with lowland highs in the lower
   60s. Temperatures look to remain slightly below normal into
   next week with midweek precipitation chances for Southwest New
   Mexico.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1100 PM MST Thu Nov 12 2026

Pacific low currently moving ashore in Southern California will 
be the primary weather factor for Friday. Ahead of it, we'll see 
high clouds moving in early Friday morning. SSW flow aloft will 
promote moisture increases overnight, with PWs jumping to 0.8" 
across South-Central New Mexico and West Texas by Friday 
afternoon. Slight negative tilting within the trough axis aloft 
and very favorable diffluent flow ahead of the system will lead to
the development of scattered showers and embedded thunderstorms 
Friday afternoon. Banded shower activity will move across much of
the region between 5PM-11PM Friday night, with a few bands 
leading to heavier rain rates and localized flooding. PoPs favor 
areas east of the Rio Grande, including El Paso, Hudspeth, and 
southern Otero Counties. Current forecast shows widespread rain 
amounts in the 0.20-0.50" range, with a few spots up to 1.00" east
of El Paso. If any flooding does occur, it'll likely occur across
West Texas.

As quick as this system arrives, it'll progress east away from us
on Saturday. Wouldn't be surprised to see some lingering rain
showers Saturday morning across South-Central New Mexico as the
system lifts out. Some of the higher elevations of the Sacramento
Mountains may even see an overnight rain/snow mix. Conditions on
Saturday will be cooler, with lowland highs only reaching the
lower 60s. We'll also see breezy west winds behind the cold front,
generally 15 to 25 mph through the afternoon hours.

Cool but dry weather expected Sunday-Monday with another shortwave
ridge in place. Temperatures will run 4 to 8 degrees below normal
for mid-November, with lowland highs in the lower 60s and some
chilly mornings in upper 30s/lower 40s.

Another shortwave trough moves across the Southern Rockies on
Tuesday. Recent model runs (both GFS and ECMWF) have shifted this
low further north, swinging it across the Four Corners. Any
precipitation chances look to miss us to the north. NBM guidance
still has mentionable rain chances for Southern New Mexico, but I
expect that to disappear in the coming days.

Long term forecast, looking at a large-scale low pressure system
over the Western US late next week. Lots of uncertainty with the 
evolution of this system, but looks like an active period. Both 
global models place the El Paso forecast area in a dry-slot, 
limiting QPF somewhat. Will keep an eye on this pattern over the 
next several days.

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 1100 PM MST Thu Nov 12 2026

VMC tonight with light, variable winds. Skies beginning clear,
with high cirrus moving in after 10Z Friday morning, bringing 
skies to SCT-BKN250. Friday afternoon will feature SCT-BKN060 
developing with scattered SHRA across all of S NM and W TX after 
00Z. Periods of MVFR CIG/VIS are expected Friday night at 
KELP/KLRU due to rain and embedded TS.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1100 AM MST Thu Nov 12 2026

No fire weather concerns through the period. Better moisture for 
Fri ahead of a disturbance with rain showers developing in the 
afternoon and seasonal temps. More widespread showers through the 
evening with a few thunderstorms possible. Rain is favored in SE 
areas. Winds pick up a bit from the S during the day, increasing 
further for Sat from W as a second storm system passes to the 
north. W winds 15-25 mph expected Sat afternoon. Low chance of 
rain/snow mix in area mtns on Sat. Cooler for Sat into next week 
as winds become lighter.

Min RHs range from 35-60% Fri, then 40-80% Sat. Vent rates will 
be mostly good to very good Sat, otherwise poor to good. 

&&
